jobs.description_text: Instawork Robotics Lab (IRL) Robots are getting smarter, but they still can’t reliably do the everyday physical tasks people do — chopping vegetables, stocking shelves, assembling parts. The bottleneck is data. UC Berkeley’s Prof. Ken Goldberg calls it the “100,000-year data gap”: the chasm between the massive text datasets used to train language models and the tiny amount of real-world, physical-dexterity data available to train robots. The entire robotics industry collected only ~100,000 hours of training data in 2024 and ~1 million in 2025 — and even the ~20 million hours projected for 2026 is still less than 0.04% of what is ultimately needed. IRL exists to close that gap. jobs.description_text: Location: Oxford, UK Office commitment: Hybrid The Role: We are looking for a highly technical Senior Software Engineer to join our System Orchestration team in System Software at Oxford Ionics. In this role, you will be responsible for building and operating the software that keeps our systems calibrated, decides what they do next and keeps the record of what they did, contributing to the team's mission of keeping our quantum computers running useful work around the clock. The trapped-ion quantum computers we are building will control 10,000 ions within two years, and all of that has to be kept in tune - settings that drift over minutes, hours and days. Without it a computer does not stop; it quietly starts producing invalid output. Calibration routines, scientists' experiments and customer workloads all compete for physical hardware, and our team builds the control plane that arbitrates that: it schedules and prioritises programs, hands exclusive access to one at a time and takes it back cooperatively, streams results while a program is still running, and keeps the record of everything that ran. It runs on every quantum computer in our fleet. Its job is to keep that machine busy and productive: running quantum programs rather than waiting in between, and running them in spec - on a machine still hitting the fidelity it is meant to hit. In this role, you will be responsible for building the software that keeps our systems calibrated, decides what they do next and keeps the record of what they did, contributing to the team's mission of keeping our quantum computers running useful work around the clock. The trapped-ion quantum computers we are building will control 10,000 ions within two years, and all of that has to be kept in tune - settings that drift over minutes, hours and days. Without it a computer does not stop; it quietly starts producing invalid output. Calibration routines, scientists' experiments and customer workloads all compete for physical hardware, and our team builds the control plane that arbitrates that: it schedules and prioritises programs, hands exclusive access to one at a time and takes it back cooperatively, streams results while a program is still running, and keeps the record of everything that ran. It runs on every quantum computer in our fleet. Its job is to keep that machine busy and productive: running quantum programs rather than waiting in between, and running them in spec - on a machine still hitting the fidelity it is meant to hit. The ambition is for that to run without a person in the loop: machines that assess their own readiness, call for the calibrations they need, and keep a full history

jobs.description_text: QA Engineer, AI-Native Quality Newton Research Research & Development Boston / Needham, MA Company Description Newton Research is a fast-growing software start-up founded by repeat entrepreneurs and well-funded by blue chip venture capital firms. About the Role Newton ships on a sprint cadence through a develop, stage and customer-environment pipeline, and the product surface is wide: conversations, blueprints, connectors, scheduled tasks, permissions and sharing, SSO, and AI agents whose behavior is not fully deterministic. A missed regression lands in front of a media planner or a customer's security review. We run everything through an AI-first lens, because it is the only way quality scales. If a quality task is repeatable, an agent does it and you supervise; if it takes judgment, that is where you spend your time. The gap this hire fills: evals and skill-change testing. Code changes already have CI and review, including PRs written by Claude. What has no safety net is behavior change: an edit to a skill, a prompt, a tool definition or a model version can silently change what our agents do, and nothing tests that today. You own that layer: curated eval sets, scoring and regression tracking, so any change to how an agent behaves is measured before it ships. Measure the AI: agent output varies run to run, so “correct” is a range you define with evals, rubrics and scoring, not an exact-match assertion. jobs.title: Software Engineer – Database Kernel
jobs.description_text: The Role: The Kernel team builds the storage engine and transaction machinery inside Neo4j. If you join us, you will not be building web APIs or shuffling data between services. Instead, you will be working directly on the database engine itself. Our day-to-day is low-level systems engineering. We write and maintain custom storage engines, the page cache, transaction handling (WAL, ACID guarantees), indexing, and memory management. The code we write determines how fast queries run across billions of nodes and relationships, and how safely data is written when a machine crashes. We are a pragmatic, engineering-led group split between Malmö and London. We read and discuss database papers (VLDB, SIGMOD, and others) to see what ideas are worth pulling into the product. We also run regular “Do What You Want” weeks so everyone has dedicated time to experiment with their own prototypes or tooling improvements. What you will actually be doing: Designing, profiling, and implementing core database features, including storage formats, index structures, and recovery paths. Diagnosing tricky concurrency bugs, race conditions, and lock contention. Performance engineering: profiling CPU, memory allocation, off-heap memory, and disk I/O to improve latency. Reviewing designs and PRs with a heavy focus on correctness, data integrity, and long-term maintainability. Helping decide technical direction and architectural trade-offs as our engine evolves. What we are looking for: Systems programming

We own Infinigraph and Composite , and we make them work as managed offerings on Aura, Neo4j’s cloud platform. Aura is Neo4j’s fully managed graph database as a service. Customers create, scale, and use Neo4j databases in the cloud without installing, clustering, or operating the database themselves. Aura runs on Kubernetes across Google Cloud, AWS, and Azure, and handles provisioning, networking, security, upgrades, and day-to-day operations for those databases. Composite is the technology behind distributed query execution in Neo4j: one query can span multiple databases. Infinigraph is our database sharding offering for large data volumes, built on a distributed database architecture. Distributed query execution is a complex and interesting topic covering query language design, performant networking, and concurrency. Those capabilities still have to run as a cloud product, and that's where a large part of this role sits: building the Go services and Kubernetes machinery that provision, scale, and operate sharded and composite clusters on Aura, reliably, at the data volumes our customers keep growing into. As part of an energetic and fun team of engineers, you'll work at the frontier of designing and implementing new capabilities for Neo4j on Aura.
